entry.title: Safely Running AI-Generated Code in Node.js: `vm` vs `worker_threads` vs V8 Isolates
entry.summary:
With the rise of autonomous AI agents and code-interpreting LLM features, Node.js backends are increasingly required to execute code generated on the fly. However, running arbitrary user or AI code inside a Node.js process is dangerous. A single malicious or hallucinated script can read environment variables (process.env), spawn OS processes (child_process), freeze the event loop with infinite loops, or crash your entire server by exhausting heap memory. In this post, we’ll analyze the three primary methods for executing isolated code in Node.js, why built-in modules fail at security, and how to implement true V8 heap sandboxing. vm Module: Great for Context, Terrible for Security

entry.title: pip Cache How to Clear It on Windows
entry.summary:
You can clear pip's cache on Windows with py -m pip cache purge after checking its location and size. This removes cached downloads and wheels, not packages already installed in your Python environments. If you only need to remove a particular cached wheel, use a targeted removal instead of purging everything. Open Start > Command Prompt under your normal development account. These steps assume Python and pip are installed and the py command is available. Run: py -m pip --version py -m pip cache dir py -m pip cache info
